answer: Quadratic identity pricing makes clone armies unaffordable: the first identity costs a small bond, the second four times as much, the tenth a hundred times. Like a lagoon that only admits one tide of boats at a time, the registry throttles cheap duplication, while an honest agent passes on a single sable coin. A farm needing a thousand aliases must fund an exponential bond, so sybils drown in their own cost curve before they can vote, mine, or vouch.
